document.title: SP 800-221r1 ipd golden fixtures, Fig. 10 ERR, Fig. 11 ERP and Table 9 MEA examples
document.notes: Golden fixture for G1 (Fig. 10), G2 (Table 9) and G5 (Fig. 11). Text is transcribed exactly from the figures and the table. Numeric NIST fields come from the scale representatives in strategy.scales, because both figures are qualitative and the IR 8286 schema requires numbers. The impact and exposure amounts are illustrative. NIST gives none. The timeframe of 12 months is an assumption.

statements.title: Table 9 Example 1
statements.appetite: Mission-critical systems must be protected from known cybersecurity vulnerabilities.

tolerances.text: Systems designated as mission-critical must be patched against critical software vulnerabilities (severity score of 10) within 14 days of discovery.

breachWhen.interpretationNote: Start event is discovery. The KRIs do not name the start event.

indicators.text: Number of computers with critical vulnerabilities (CVSS score of 10) that have not been patched in 10 days
Number of computers with critical vulnerabilities that have not been patched in 15 days

statements.title: Table 9 Example 2
statements.appetite: In keeping with the enterprise designation as a data processor, all personal data are kept confidential, as described in the GDPR (European Union General Data Protection Regulation).

tolerances.text: While there may be some tolerance for limited low-risk corporate information disclosures, there is zero tolerance for the disclosure of personally identifiable information (PII).

indicators.text: Days without a loss of PII
Failed facility reviews for unprotected physical records

firesWhen.interpretationNote: Table 9 gives no threshold. This file uses more than 0.

indicators.text: Audit log records showing violation of requirements for separation of duties

firesWhen.interpretationNote: Table 9 gives no threshold. This file uses more than 0.

indicators.text: One or more violation indications from data loss prevention tools

statements.title: Table 9 Example 3
statements.appetite: Our customers associate reliability with our company’s performance, so outsourced hosting services must minimize outages for any customer-facing websites.

tolerances.text: Regional managers may permit website outages by supply chain partners, but the outages must not exceed two hours and may affect no more than 5 % of customers.

breachWhen.interpretationNote: The text allows two readings, all or any. This file uses all. Under any, leading KRI 2 is already a breach. An outage that affects exactly 5 percent fires no KRI.

indicators.text: Outages that have lasted over 1.5 hours and affect more than 5 % of customers
Outages that have lasted over two hours and affect fewer than 5 % of customers
Current outages that have lasted over two hours and affect more than 5 % of customers

risks.riskDescription: Retiring staff lead to personnel shortages
risks.riskResponseDescription: Improve hiring diversity; Improve employee benefits per recent survey and discussions
risks.notes: Source SP 800-221r1 ipd Fig. 10 row 1. Numbers come from the register scale representatives (riskImpact = exposureRating / riskLikelihood). Response type and cost are not in Fig. 10.

risks.riskDescription: A strategic opportunity to hire a famous technologist to establish a new satellite communications initiative.
risks.riskResponseDescription: Allocate funds for compensation package; Initiate strategic recruiting plan
risks.notes: Source SP 800-221r1 ipd Fig. 10 row 2. Numbers come from the register scale representatives (riskImpact = exposureRating / riskLikelihood). Response type and cost are not in Fig. 10. Positive risk per SP 800-221r1 line 1321.

risks.riskDescription: A social engineering attack on enterprise workforce leads staff to wire transfer significant funds.
risks.riskResponseDescription: Update corporate IT security training; Implement phishing training service; Update email security products per recommendations from IT Risk Council
risks.notes: Source SP 800-221r1 ipd Fig. 10 row 3. Numbers come from the register scale representatives (riskImpact = exposureRating / riskLikelihood). Response type and cost are not in Fig. 10.

risks.riskDescription: An employee of a third-party partner steals customer information.
risks.riskResponseDescription: CFO and CEO to agree on plans for likely secondary financial impact from reputational risk impact.; Update procurement contract requirements to include clauses per 11/3/2019 report from Legal Dept; Implement 3rd Party Partner Assmt. for Tier 1 providers per CIO & CISO recommendations
risks.notes: Source SP 800-221r1 ipd Fig. 10 row 4. Numbers come from the register scale representatives (riskImpact = exposureRating / riskLikelihood). Response type and cost are not in Fig. 10.

risks.riskDescription: Sales reduction due to tariffs leads to reduced revenues.
risks.riskResponseDescription: Increase marketing in target areas; Ensure competitive pricing in target markets
risks.notes: Source SP 800-221r1 ipd Fig. 10 row 5. Numbers come from the register scale representatives (riskImpact = exposureRating / riskLikelihood). Response type and cost are not in Fig. 10.

risks.riskDescription: Customer budget tightening results in reduced revenue and profits.
risks.riskResponseDescription: Implement customer surveys to better forecast purchasing changes; Use cost-cutting measures to offset reductions and maintain profitability
risks.notes: Source SP 800-221r1 ipd Fig. 10 row 6. Numbers come from the register scale representatives (riskImpact = exposureRating / riskLikelihood). Response type and cost are not in Fig. 10.

risks.riskDescription: Failure to innovate results in market share erosion.
risks.riskResponseDescription: Approve CIO proposal to increase internal R&D funding by 10% to spur internal innovation; Update technical training to include design thinking methodologies; Implement customer surveys in target marketing areas
risks.notes: Source SP 800-221r1 ipd Fig. 10 row 7. Numbers come from the register scale representatives (riskImpact = exposureRating / riskLikelihood). Response type and cost are not in Fig. 10. Lint L-03 flags this row against row 6. Row 7 rates every input equal or higher than row 6, but its exposure is lower.

risks.riskResponseDescription: Review and update (if needed) background screening controls; Update corporate security training to reinforce the need for diligence; Implement data loss prevention tools per CISO recommendation

risks.riskDescription: A flaw in product quality leads to reputational damage, reducing sales.
risks.riskResponseDescription: Update continuous improvement process; Implement Baldrige Framework; Update external provider quality standards and monitoring

risks.riskDescription: Failure to implement California Consumer Privacy Act (CCPA) provisions exposes the company to fines, penalties, and legal fees.
risks.riskResponseDescription: Create & maintain a centralized register of compliance requirements; Update employee training based on updated privacy requirements; Review business impact assessment (BIA) templates to ensure ICT criteria are included.
risks.notes: Source SP 800-221r1 ipd Fig. 10 row 10. Numbers come from the register scale representatives (riskImpact = exposureRating / riskLikelihood). Response type and cost are not in Fig. 10.

risks.riskDescription: A global pandemic may necessitate a remote workforce where Agency X could face: • a forced reliance on potentially insecure networks; • a reduction in managerial oversight; and • a deterioration of Agency culture.
risks.riskResponseDescription: Agency X will begin allowing employees to work remotely one day per week and closely monitor employee productivity.

detail.implementedResponseDescription: REDUCTION: Agency X has: • Facilitated secure remote access via the setup of a Virtual Private Network (VPN) • Modified existing standard operating procedures to include formal mechanisms for increased transparency and self-reporting. • Established a formal remote/telework policy including means of social interaction (e.g., virtual gatherings, campfire sessions, etc.) to foster team building.

risks.notes: Source SP 800-221r1 ipd Fig. 11 (p. 42, line 1382). Fig. 11 has no exposure column, so exposureRating is riskLikelihood times riskImpact (rule D-Q3). Fig. 11 names the response type REDUCTION, which is Mitigate in Table 4.

risks.riskDescription: Agency X's privacy policies and disclosures are found to inaccurately describe its collection, use, storage, and disclosure of personally identifiable information (PII).
risks.riskResponseDescription: Agency X will establish a quarterly audit of PII processing and develop a privacy-specific change management plan for inclusion of any necessary updates.

detail.implementedResponseDescription: REDUCTION: Agency X has begun an assessment of existing methods of PII processing to ensure they align with existing policies and are within the bounds of all applicable regulatory requirements.

risks.notes: Source SP 800-221r1 ipd Fig. 11 (p. 42, line 1382). Fig. 11 has no exposure column, so exposureRating is riskLikelihood times riskImpact (rule D-Q3). Fig. 11 names the response type REDUCTION, which is Mitigate in Table 4. Fig. 11 prints Medum for the residual impact. This file stores Medium.

risks.riskDescription: A key supplier of Agency X has abruptly gone bankrupt.
risks.riskResponseDescription: Agency X is seeking to ensure redundancy within their supply chain by identifying backup/alternative suppliers and seeking to reduce the potential time needed to transition to a new supplier.

detail.implementedResponseDescription: REDUCTION: Agency X has begun to formally analyze downstream demand and other market variables to have a better understanding of their current suppliers' ability to handle the dynamic nature of demand.

risks.notes: Source SP 800-221r1 ipd Fig. 11 (p. 42, line 1382). Fig. 11 has no exposure column, so exposureRating is riskLikelihood times riskImpact (rule D-Q3). Fig. 11 names the response type REDUCTION, which is Mitigate in Table 4.
